text:
alyssa: Heads-up — after the docs migration I'm seeing a bunch of 404s from anchor/heading mismatches in the SDK reference pages. Example: /sdk/python/#client-init now 404s. CI linkcheck flagged ~14 broken anchors. Anyone on it?

mario: I can take a pass on anchor normalization. Is this the sphinx -> docusaurus conversion where :ref: links became plain relative links? We need to map old anchor names to the new slugified headings.

alyssa: Yep. Some headings had parentheses, slashes, or emojis which changed the slug. Also some headings were translated to sentence case which changed the anchor.

sam: Can you paste a short linkcheck snippet so I can see the failing pattern?

alyssa: Sure — here's a sample from the CI job:```
docs/sdk/python/index.md: broken link foo: /sdk/python/#client-init -> 404
docs/sdk/go/clients.md: broken link bar: /sdk/go/#creating-a-client (expected /sdk/go/#creating-a-client)
Total broken anchors: 14
```

mario: Two options: 1) add explicit HTML anchors/frontmatter slugs to the problematic MDX headers (quick, localized fix) 2) add a redirect/alias map so old anchor URLs redirect to new anchors (better for external links). I can prototype both.

jen: I prefer redirects so external docs that reference the old anchors don't break. But explicit anchors are fine as a stopgap. Also we should add a small normalization script to avoid regressions on future conversions.

mario: Plan: run a slugify script over the repo to detect mismatches, then add frontmatter 'slug' or explicit {#anchor} for the top offenders, and add a docsRedirects entry in docusaurus config for legacy anchors. Opening a PR now.

sam: If you add explicit anchors in MDX, use the fenced syntax so Docusaurus picks it up: `### Client initialization {#client-init}`. For frontmatter slugs, add `slug: /sdk/python/#client-init` if necessary.

mario: Example fix I pushed in the branch — small MDX tweak:```
- ### Client initialization
+ ### Client initialization {#client-init}
```
Also adding a mapping in config:```
// docusaurus.config.js (snippet)
module.exports = {
  // ...
  plugins: [
    ['@redwood/docs-redirects', {
      redirects: [
        {from: '/sdk/python/#client-init', to: '/sdk/python/#client-init'},
        {from: '/sdk/go/#creating-client-old', to: '/sdk/go/#creating-a-client'}
      ]
    }]
  ]
}
```

alyssa: Nice. Can you also add test coverage for linkcheck? Run the local command so maintainers can reproduce: `yarn docs:linkcheck` (or `poetry run mkdocs build && mkdocs linkcheck` for old toolchain).

mario: Done. I ran `yarn docs:linkcheck` locally, addressed the top 10 failures, and pushed PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/468 with commits. Latest commit: abc123def.

deploy-bot: CI: linkcheck job started for PR #468. (checks: lint, build, linkcheck)

jen: Reviewing PR now :eyes: — please include a short changelog note about the redirects so support can reply to customer tickets.

sam: Quick nit — please normalize anchor names to kebab-case (no underscores) in the script. Otherwise LGTM.

mario: Good call, updated the script and added a small unit test. Pushed commit abc123def2. Asking for review from @jen and @sam.

jen: Approved. :thumbsup: I'll wait for CI green to merge.

deploy-bot: CI: linkcheck passed, all checks green for PR #468.

mario: Merged and deployed the docs site. Commit merged: abc123def3.

deploy-bot: production deploy complete. Post-deploy linkcheck: 0 broken anchors found.

alyssa: Huge thanks everyone — that fixed the SDK anchor issues and the customer 404s. :tada: If anyone sees new anchor fails, please drop them here with the `yarn docs:linkcheck` output.

sam: Also adding a short migration note to the docs migration guide about how we slugify headings and where redirects live.

jen: Great, closing the loop.
